generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Reed College's account of the family, with Michigan State's Botany Online and the Sydney eFlora, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): flowers three-merous and zygomorphic; three sepals, one of them dorsal, and three petals, the median one the labellum or lip; in most orchid flowers the ovary twists 180 degrees, bringing the lip to the bottom; stamens, style and stigma joined in one column, usually with one fertile anther (two in the lady's slippers); ovary inferior, of three carpels.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 405 Orchidaceae: perennial herbs, on the ground, on trees, or living on fungi; leaves undivided, alternate and often in two ranks, rarely opposite, sometimes all reduced to scales, sheathing at the base.
